smote.what: Oversampling by interpolating between neighbors of the minority class (SMOTE by Chawla et al., via imbalanced-learn).
smote.good_for: Imbalanced datasets with 2+ classes and numeric features; very fast, no GPU (TABULAR_STATO.md).
smote.avoid_when: With a single class imblearn is not applicable: the wrapper interpolates KNN neighbors (native, not imblearn). Other cases: not documented.

fair-smote.what: SMOTE that removes biased labels and rebalances examples by the sensitive attribute, equal between positive and negative class (FSE 2021).
fair-smote.good_for: Reducing bias on sensitive attributes (sex, race, age) in datasets with a target of 2+ classes (Fair-SMOTE README).
fair-smote.avoid_when: Datasets with a single class: the wrapper falls back to KNN interpolation without fairness (FALLBACK status). The target is assumed to be the last column.

smote-cdnn.what: SMOTE followed by cleaning with Edited CDNN (hybrid multi-class sampling, imbalanced-learn API).
smote-cdnn.good_for: Imbalanced multi-class datasets (the README mentions multi-class hybrid sampling). No performance is attributed here.
smote-cdnn.avoid_when: Datasets with a single class: the wrapper uses SMOTE without CDNN (FALLBACK).

goggle.what: Generative model (ICLR 2023) that learns the relational structure between variables and generates data that respects it.
goggle.good_for: Tabular data with dependencies between variables; allows adding prior knowledge and regularization on the dependencies (README).

castgan.what: Cascaded GAN for realistic synthesis of tabular data (CasTGAN).
castgan.good_for: Not documented beyond the paper title (realistic tabular synthesis).
castgan.avoid_when: Not documented. The README mentions a *_train.csv file and optionally *_dtypes.pkl with the column types, recommended.

tabfairgan.what: WGAN for tabular data, with or without a fairness constraint.
tabfairgan.good_for: Generating synthetic data with a fairness constraint (README); without the constraint it only generates quality data.
tabfairgan.avoid_when: The fairness constraint requires a configuration with a sensitive attribute; the benchmark wrapper does not document it, not verified.

cuts.what: Customizable tabular synthesis (ICML 2024): statistical and logical constraints can be imposed through a program.
cuts.good_for: When constraints must be imposed on the generated data (README example: E[age|age>30]==40).
cuts.avoid_when: In the benchmark the wrapper uses the Denoiser with one-hot encoded data; the use of constraints is not documented. Other limits: not documented.

tabular-argn.what: Autoregressive framework for tabular synthesis (TabularARGN), run with mostlyai-engine.
tabular-argn.good_for: Not documented beyond the paper (high fidelity, flexible). Reference implementation Apache-2.0.
tabular-argn.avoid_when: In envs/argn torch is CPU-only, so it runs on CPU (slower: 37.6 s on 49 rows, 1 epoch).

prefair.what: Private synthetic generation (differential privacy, PrivBayes) that is also fair (PreFair, VLDB 2023).
prefair.good_for: When differential privacy and fairness on a sensitive attribute are both needed.
prefair.avoid_when: In the benchmark the sensitive attribute is chosen heuristically (column name sex/gender/race/age, otherwise the first column with few values), epsilon is fixed at 10, and it is slow (45.9 s on 49 rows) because of DataSynthesizer's multiprocessing.

ddpm.what: TabDDPM: diffusion model for tabular data (ICML 2023).
ddpm.good_for: Not documented in the repo beyond the paper title.
ddpm.avoid_when: Not documented. The wrapper uses the last column as the target.

ctabgan.what: CTAB-GAN baseline run from the TabDDPM repository (conditional GAN for tabular data).
ctabgan.avoid_when: Not documented. In the benchmark it runs via the TabDDPM worker, not from Algorithms/CTAB-GAN-Plus.

ctabgan-plus.what: CTAB-GAN+: GAN for tabular synthesis, improved version of CTAB-GAN (without the differential privacy part in this code).
ctabgan-plus.good_for: The repo has examples for classification (Adult) and regression (king).
ctabgan-plus.avoid_when: The README lists old dependencies (torch 1.9.1, sklearn 0.24.1, for BayesianGaussianMixture). In the benchmark it runs via the TabDDPM worker. Other cases: not documented.

tvae.what: VAE for tabular data, run from the TabDDPM repository (baseline).

syrfd.what: SyRFDRes: synthesis that uses relaxed functional dependencies (RFDs) discovered on the dataset as constraints.
syrfd.good_for: Datasets for which RFD files exist (discovered_rfds_processed folder); the v8 version scales to large datasets.
syrfd.avoid_when: Without RFD files for the dataset the run fails, unless --allow-fallback is set (then FALLBACK to empty RFDs). There is no README.

tabsyn.what: Score-based diffusion in the latent space of a VAE for mixed-type tabular data (ICLR 2024).
tabsyn.good_for: Mixed numeric and categorical data (paper title).
tabsyn.avoid_when: In the benchmark the wrapper maps epochs onto VAE and diffusion steps (wrapper choice). Other limits: not documented.

tabdiff.what: Diffusion model for mixed-type tabular data (ICLR 2025).
tabdiff.good_for: Mixed numeric and categorical data (paper title).
tabdiff.avoid_when: In the benchmark TabDiff's internal metrics and plots are disabled. Other limits: not documented.

octree.what: Feature generation for tabular data via an LLM reasoning over decision trees (OCTree). It does not produce rows.
octree.avoid_when: Requires an LLM (local Llama-2-7B, about 13 GB at 4 bit, or API). In the benchmark, without an LLM only a surrogate runs (FALLBACK), not OCTree.

harmonic.what: Tabular synthesis with an LLM fine-tuned (LoRA) on instructions built from the k neighbors, to discover relations between rows; it aims to reduce privacy risk.
harmonic.good_for: Synthesis with large LLMs and privacy-risk assessment (README).
harmonic.avoid_when: Requires fine-tuning a 7B LLM: needs a GPU with more than 8 GB or quantization. Without an LLM only a surrogate runs (FALLBACK), not HARMONIC.

synthetic-llm.what: EPIC: prompting an LLM (OpenAI API) to synthesize samples of imbalanced classes in tabular classification.
synthetic-llm.good_for: Tabular classification with imbalanced classes (title and README).
synthetic-llm.avoid_when: Requires an OpenAI API key and paid online calls. Without them only a surrogate runs (FALLBACK), not EPIC.

kamino.what: Synthesis with differential privacy that respects the integrity constraints (Denial Constraints) of the dataset.
kamino.good_for: Datasets for which Denial Constraints are available; preserves structure and correlations.
kamino.avoid_when: The dataset's DC file is required (missing for some datasets). In the benchmark a Python reimplementation runs (workers/kamino_engine.py), not the original code (which requires Docker, PostgreSQL and conda): to be considered FALLBACK.
kamino.source: Algorithms/kamino-master/README.md; TABULAR_STATO.md; the project notes; workers/run_algo_worker.py
